speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough going on for about two months now. It's productive, and the phlegm is usually greenish, though I haven't seen any blood. However, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That green phlegm suggests an infection; have you noticed any fever, night sweats, or unintended weight loss during these two months? Also, does your shortness of breath worsen when you lie flat or climb stairs?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't had a fever, night sweats, or lost any weight. The shortness of breath mainly happens when I climb stairs or exert myself, but I don't feel worse when lying flat. I want to emphasize that, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; the absence of orthopnea and constitutional symptoms makes heart failure less likely. Given the productive green sputum and exertional dyspnea, do you have a history of smoking or recent exposure to dust or chemicals? Also, have you noticed any swelling in your ankles or legs recently?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I've been smoking for about 25 years and I work as a mechanic, so I'm exposed to dust and chemicals daily. I haven't noticed any swelling in my ankles or legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) with acute exacerbation.
